where: blaze: the identity of a function that coerces to `dyn` (hir-ty-identity, `vtable` in facts.rs) against the vtable the code generator gives it as data
what: The oracle (crates/hir-ty-codegen/v2/edits/revisions.rs, `any_turn_sequence_builds_as_clean`) on its first run, 40 sequences, shrank a failure to one turn: an impl that has the trait`s required method is given its own copy of a provided one. `app::shapes` (`by_dyn(&A) ^ by_dyn(&B)`) keeps its kernel key c585c7ccc358, in a clean build of each revision in a database of its own, and its record differs: the vtable of `B` it holds as data names its slots by instance key (before: `sides` 418cb86c8ef4, the same instance `A`s slot has, `area` 641d00bf623a; after: 7fbf4557068a and 31cdc9d8da77), the data id moves (f0b246844056 to ec4a616d212e) and the relocation to it. Code and lines equal. With the store check on the build stops (`BLAZE_VERIFY_STORE: the store`s value of app::shapes ... is not what computing it again gives`); with it off the stale record is taken and the old vtable linked. The existing case an_impl_overriding_a_provided_method_changes_its_vtable passes with one key too (735b7f2d7e0b both revisions), so there the bytes are equal: what differs here is a second impl sharing the provided method`s instance and a required method whose instance key moves when the override is put above it.
cost: a wrong program when the store check does not sample the hit; found in 45 s of the oracle
cause: not found: either `vtable` is not reached for this coercion or what it hashes of a slot (`name(method, args)`) is not what the data names (an instance key that two impls share for a provided method, and that moves with the method`s place in its impl)
whys: the record holds the vtable`s bytes and slot targets, the key holds names
the key and the record are written by two walks of the same body that nothing holds to each other for function data (relocs_hashed.rs does it for constants and statics only)
class: a key and its value derived by two code paths
prevention: one walk yields both the record`s references and the key`s parts (the key is a hash of the references the emitter actually wrote), or a test like relocs_hashed for function data; until then the oracle`s case an_override_beside_a_required_method_changes_the_vtable holds it, known under sim
workaround: none; BLAZE_VERIFY_STORE=1 turns the wrong program into a stopped build
state: open, for the lane that owns hir-ty-identity: the case replays in 0.5 s (`cargo test -p hir-ty-codegen --lib -- an_override_beside`), `the_keys_of_the_coercion_site_before_and_after_the_override --ignored --nocapture` prints both revisions` relocations and data
